entries.definition_short: Canonical specialized boundary-control agent named in the publishable specification.
entries.definition_operational: The agent identity fixed by the specification. It controls frontier interactions and exchanges, validates, filters, blocks, quarantines, and releases boundary artifacts under fail-closed governance.

entries.definition_short: Agent role for ingress, egress, persistence, and transport-adjacent artifact exchange.
entries.definition_operational: Used for the agent role and identity class. The term frames the agent as a boundary-governed component rather than a general-purpose executor.

entries.definition_short: The governed core whose boundary is controlled by the agent.

entries.definition_short: Logical boundary spanning runtime I/O, persistence commits, and transport of artifacts.
entries.definition_operational: The boundary delimits the governed exchange surface. The agent evaluates artifacts that cross this boundary and applies explicit contracts, validators, and evidence-linked decisions before visibility or release.

entries.definition_short: Any input, output, tool-state payload, or persistence/transport-adjacent object that attempts to cross the controlled boundary.
entries.definition_operational: The base boundary object class for the specification. The semantic invariant states that no boundary artifact acquires execution, persistence, or transport visibility without explicit validation evidence appropriate to its class.

entries.definition_short: The boundary that artifacts attempt to cross under agent governance.
entries.definition_operational: Used in the defining statement and in the operational definition of Boundary artifact. The term identifies the governed crossing point for runtime, persistence, and transport-adjacent exchange.

entries.definition_short: Persistence-side actions included in the logical boundary.

entries.definition_short: Runtime input and output side of the governed boundary.

entries.definition_short: Transport-side movement of artifacts governed by the boundary model.

entries.definition_short: Mandatory fail-closed handling at specified failure and escalation conditions.
entries.definition_operational: The policy is mandatory at schema failure, allowlist failure, CPW critical escalation, evidence failure, counter replay, or authority exhaustion. It is also reflected in gate logic, workflow, and failure semantics.

entries.definition_short: Approval channel in the escalation path for approval-required handling.

entries.definition_short: Active policy profile bound into request and decision handling.

entries.definition_short: Controlled restoration of a previously blocked or quarantined path after all mandatory validators, approvals, and anchors are satisfied.
entries.definition_operational: Readmission is the restoration control used after remediation. The authority record defines readmission triggers, the temporal contract defines when readmission is legal, and the workflow emits READMIT when restoration succeeds.

entries.definition_short: State in which finalization prerequisites are checked by the evidence gate and reconstruction-linked validators.

entries.definition_short: State in which the agent is ready to receive input or returns after successful release, readmission, or hold exit.

entries.definition_short: State in which ingress input is validated against mandatory checks.
entries.definition_operational: Entered after INPUT_RECEIVED. The workflow uses this state for VAL-01, VAL-02, VAL-03, and related failure handling before block or review.

Boundary Defense Agent — Specification / Workflow / State-Transition Record

entries.definition_short: Audit-only posture in which no compliance-claimed finalization is permitted until evidence prerequisites are restored.
entries.definition_operational: The workflow enters NONCOMPLIANT_HOLD when VAL-05 or VAL-08 fails at finalization review. The same token also appears in gate logic and semantic contract as a gate status and verdict token.

entries.definition_short: State in which the path remains blocked and no further release occurs.
entries.definition_operational: Reached on validation failure, CPW critical handling, and other blocking conditions. Readmission may return the path to IDLE after remediation.

entries.definition_short: State in which the release path is prepared with validator context and policy scope.
entries.definition_operational: Entered when no escalation condition remains or when approval is granted on a quarantined tool-state path. FINALIZATION_REQUESTED moves the path to finalization review.

entries.definition_short: State in which a tool-state path is preserved for inspection but not released.
entries.definition_operational: Entered when tool-state is present and elevated boundary risk is classified. Approval evidence is required before the path can move to READY_FOR_RELEASE.

entries.definition_short: Primary event token for approval denial on an approval-required path.

entries.definition_short: Workflow event for successful approval on a quarantined path.

Boundary Defense Agent — Specification / Workflow / State-Transition Record

entries.definition_short: Workflow event for restored evidence prerequisites on a hold path.

entries.definition_short: Primary event token for counter replay in the semantic core summary.
